Class ResteasyCdiExtension

java.lang.Object
org.jboss.resteasy.cdi.ResteasyCdiExtension
All Implemented Interfaces:
jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.Extension
public class ResteasyCdiExtension extends Object implements jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.Extension
A CDI Extension that integrates Jakarta REST components with CDI. This extension:
  • Assigns default scopes to discovered Jakarta REST resources (RequestScoped), providers (ApplicationScoped), and Application subclasses (ApplicationScoped)
  • Adds @Inject to @Context-annotated fields, setter methods, and constructors so that CDI can inject context values
  • Registers the @Context and @Default beans for the Jakarta REST context types
  • Wraps InjectionTarget instances for Jakarta REST components within JaxrsInjectionTarget to handle property injection and validation
  • Builds the session bean interface map used by CdiInjectorFactory for EJB lookup
  • Tracks CDI-managed Jakarta REST components in the ResteasyBeanContainer
Author:
Jozef Hartinger, James R. Perkins

    • validateProviderScope

      public void validateProviderScope(@Observes jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.ProcessManagedBean<?> event)
      Fails the deployment if a provider is explicitly declared @Dependent. Providers are application singletons, while each injection of a @Dependent bean creates a new instance. A provider which declares type variables is excluded, as CDI requires such a bean to be @Dependent. Session beans are excluded, as an unscoped session bean is made @Dependent.
      Parameters:
      event - the managed bean being processed

    • registerContextProducers

      public void registerContextProducers(@Observes jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.AfterBeanDiscovery event, jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.BeanManager beanManager)
      Registers producers for the Jakarta REST context types, the Application and the Jakarta Servlet types which are required to be injectable.

      The Jakarta REST context types are owned by the implementation, so the @Context and @Default beans are always registered. For the Application and the Servlet types, the @Default bean is only registered if no other bean already provides the type.

      Parameters:
      event - the after bean discovery event
      beanManager - the bean manager

    • observeProviderContracts

      public <T> void observeProviderContracts(@Observes jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.ProcessAnnotatedType<T> event, jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.BeanManager beanManager)
      Adds @Inject to the @Context injection points of a discovered type which implements a provider contract, is not annotated with @Provider and does not declare a scope. Such a type is made an @ApplicationScoped provider, or a @Singleton provider if the type cannot be proxied, in observeBeanAttributes(ProcessBeanAttributes, BeanManager). Providers are application singletons, while such a type would otherwise be @Dependent. This can only happen when the type is discovered without a bean defining annotation, e.g. in a bean-discovery-mode="all" archive, and is registered as a provider through Application.getClasses() or a Feature.

      Only types with a @Context annotation are observed, as other types have no injection points to change. The scope of all such types is set in observeBeanAttributes(ProcessBeanAttributes, BeanManager).

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type
      Parameters:
      event - the annotated type being processed
      beanManager - the bean manager

    • observeBeanAttributes

      public <T> void observeBeanAttributes(@Observes jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.ProcessBeanAttributes<T> event, jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.BeanManager beanManager)
      Decides the scope of the resources, providers and Application subclasses recorded when their annotated type was processed, and whether they are managed by CDI, i.e. added to the bean container. This is only invoked for beans, so a type which is not a bean, e.g. one with a constructor CDI cannot satisfy, is not added to the bean container and is created by RESTEasy.

      The @Path, @Provider and @ApplicationPath stereotypes may define the default scopes. The same defaults are set if no scope is defined, e.g. if the annotations are not stereotypes in the environment or @Path is only present on methods. In addition:

      • A resource which does not define a scope is made @RequestScoped. An unproxyable resource which does not declare a scope is made @Dependent, which does not require a client proxy and is still created for each request.
      • A @Provider which does not define a scope is made @ApplicationScoped. An unproxyable one which does not declare a scope is made @Singleton, which does not require a client proxy.
      • A provider without @Provider which does not declare a scope is made @ApplicationScoped, or @Singleton if it cannot be proxied.
      • A resource or provider which declares type variables and does not declare a scope is made @Dependent, as CDI requires for a bean whose type contains type variables. RESTEasy still creates a single instance of such a provider.
      • An Application subclass which does not declare a scope, e.g. without @ApplicationPath, is made @ApplicationScoped.
      A warning is logged when the default scope of the @Path or @Provider stereotype is overridden, as the application should declare the scope.
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type
      Parameters:
      event - the bean attributes being processed
      beanManager - the bean manager

    • observeApplications

      public <T extends jakarta.ws.rs.core.Application> void observeApplications(@Observes jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.ProcessAnnotatedType<T> event, jakarta.enterprise.inject.spi.BeanManager beanManager)
      Adds @Inject to the @Context injection points of Application subclasses and records them, so their scope and whether they are managed by CDI can be decided in observeBeanAttributes(ProcessBeanAttributes, BeanManager).
